## Context

**What this card is.** Two files that make the operational loop ALERT-DRIVEN
instead of hand-run: `observability/prometheus.yml` (the Prometheus scrape
configuration for this repo's local backend) and `observability/alerts.yaml`,
which is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every alert name and every metric name
referenced anywhere else in this milestone. If a name is not in
`observability/alerts.yaml`, it does not exist in this milestone.

**The measured base state (measured at groom on the pinned BASE, not assumed).**

- `observability/` exists at the BASE and holds EXACTLY two files, both t75's:
  `README.md` (blob `d7d40e8d5521b60a64f9daed4a533ad6b845cac0`) and
  `compose.yaml` (blob `f3e609aaa2c651973ad469bdc0423f344dc0e4c1`). Both are
  byte-pinned by ac5 and this card may not touch either (second-writer rule).
- **DISPATCH-BODY CORRECTION, measured:** the dispatch brief and the survey
  draft both say "`alerts.yaml` exists and `prometheus.yml` must point at it".
  That is WRONG. `git log --all --oneline -- observability/alerts.yaml` and
  `... -- observability/prometheus.yml` are BOTH EMPTY - neither file exists
  anywhere in this repository's history, and at the BASE `observability/`
  holds only the two t75 files. This card therefore CREATES BOTH files, which
  is exactly what its Constraints section already says ("Exactly 2 files:
  `observability/prometheus.yml`, `observability/alerts.yaml`"). No behaviour
  changes; the survey AC text was written against a state that never existed.
- `observability/compose.yaml` mounts ONLY
  `./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro` (line 26). It mounts NO
  alerts file, so a `rule_files: [/etc/prometheus/alerts.yaml]` reference
  resolves to a path that does not exist inside the container. Consequence if
  left alone: Prometheus starts and evaluates ZERO rules (a missing rule file
  is not a crash - it is silence). Per the Constraints this is recorded as a
  FOLLOW-UP (see "Out of scope"); this card does NOT edit t75's compose file.
- The fallback condition is a merged, measurable payload, not a hypothesis:
  `backend/app/routers/health.py` lines 7-8 emit `fallback_active` and set
  `status` to `"degraded"` exactly when a fallback is active, and
  `backend/app/database.py` line 40 `is_fallback()` is the latch.
- `backend/app/telemetry.py` does NOT exist at the BASE (`git show
  2a9274851fbb67bf8c1589ce3556b4e8ac11f0a3:backend/app/telemetry.py` -> "exists on disk, but not in
  2a9274851fbb67bf8c1589ce3556b4e8ac11f0a3"); it landed on the tip with the t78 merge. `APP_VERSION = "1.0.0"`
  and `ENVIRONMENT: Literal["development", "production"] = "development"` are
  measured at `backend/app/config.py` lines 42-43 at the BASE, which is why
  the two pinned annotation values are `version: "1.0.0"` and
  `environment: development`.
- Zero name collisions at the BASE: a bounded grep of the scope B' product
  trees (below) for `DBFallbackActive`, `HighExpenseCreationFailures` and the
  four metric names returns NO hits (measured rc=1 on both scan legs). Every
  fence is RED at the BASE because both files are absent there.
- No Prometheus/Alertmanager binary is required by any gate: `command -v
  promtool` is NOT found on the grooming host, and no fence downloads one. The
  validators are YAML-parse and rule-shape legs plus a parse-level expression
  evaluator, never a live-server leg.

**Supervisor decision, recorded verbatim as required (Option B, approved
2026-10-16).** `DBFallbackActive` reads the declared 0/1 GAUGE
`db_fallback_active`, NOT `up{job="backend"} == 0`. The three candidate
options were ranked and the supervisor independently verified the claims on
merged-t78 bytes: option A (`up == 0`) "is a liveness rule wearing a fallback
name, exactly the attested-by-reference defect this milestone exists to
remove"; option C (a rule over a series nobody emits) is "a never-fireable
dangling rule"; option B is "the only option that keeps t79's own extraction AC
satisfiable", and t77's card already defers to "whatever series carries the
fallback state, which t76's inventory names". The mandatory conditions of that
approval, all honoured by this card: (1) this disclosure appears verbatim;
this is the ONE place the authority adds a name (`db_fallback_active`) beyond
the plan's three-counter template, and it lands inside t79's ALREADY-ASSIGNED
file envelope (`backend/app/telemetry.py`, a callback gauge on the merged
`is_fallback()` latch - no new files, no new ports, no new services, no edit
to `database.py`); (2) the machine-readable `# METRIC-INVENTORY` stays exactly
the 4-name emit-set (`expense_created_total`, `expense_create_failures_total`,
`category_created_total`, `db_fallback_active`) with NO external-metrics
section, and ac3's subset leg stays exception-free; (3) the `DBFallbackActive`
expr is pinned to `db_fallback_active == 1` with `for: 5m` and
`HighExpenseCreationFailures` is untouched; (4) `db_fallback_active` is a GAUGE
and the inventory says so, so t77's panel type and t79's instrument type agree
- **t79 MUST emit it or t79 fails its own extraction AC: this card DECLARES,
t79 IMPLEMENTS, per the plan's declare/match doctrine; this is not t79 scope
creep**; (5) ac2's non-vacuity proof evaluates the pinned rules against a
SYNTHESIZED `db_fallback_active` series at parse level (no promtool exists on
this host and no network download is permitted) - the rule must fire on a
value-1 sample and must not fire on a value-0 sample - and end-to-end firing
is demonstrated in the t84 drill via `--simulate-fallback`; (6) the decision

**Supervisor decision, scan scope B' (approved 2026-10-16, recorded as
required).** ac3's "no other file may invent a name" leg does NOT scan the
whole tree. It scans an ENUMERATED bounded scope - `backend/app`,
`backend/tests`, `frontend/src`, `scripts`, `e2e`, `docker-compose.yml`,
`render.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile` - using the CONCRETE names read out of
`observability/alerts.yaml` (alert names as plain substrings; metric names in
Prometheus exposition context: `name{`, `name <digit>`, or `# TYPE name`), and
it excludes `observability/**` (the authority itself) and
`backend/app/telemetry.py` (t79's permitted code-side mirror). Rationale for
the bounded scope, measured: `.git` is ~65 MB and the `node_modules`/venv trees
are large, so a full-tree recursive grep with global excludes is what pushed an
earlier call past the tool timeout. A full-tree scan is NOT required to prove
the claim, because the plan's own file envelopes put every future consumer
inside the enumerated paths.

**What this card is NOT.** It adds no port and no service (the 9090/9093/3000
band and the service set are t75's), no dependency, no backend code, no
`openapi.yaml` change (FROZEN), and no edit to `observability/compose.yaml` or
`observability/README.md`. The `/metrics` endpoint this scrape config reads is
t78's and its schema exemption is recorded in t78's card, not here.

## Acceptance criteria

Five criteria - within max_acs=6. Each is one deterministic `bash -c`
one-liner run from the repository root (worktree), with exactly two single
quotes, no backtick, no heredoc, pure ASCII. All five were EXECUTED at the
pinned BASE in a throwaway clone by this groom and are RED there for the named
reason (table under "Verification commands"). Each fence stages a python3 probe
to `/tmp` from an embedded base64 payload (the t65/t78/t80 precedent) so no
complex logic lives in the one-liner, and each fence carries its own
non-vacuity control: ac1/ac2/ac3 run in-fence positive controls (an adversarial
document or a planted file that MUST be rejected/found), ac4 runs in-fence
mutation controls, and ac5's six planted-violation controls were measured by
this groom against the same fence bytes.

### ac1 - both files exist, parse, and the scrape config is provably the local shape

`observability/prometheus.yml` and `observability/alerts.yaml` both exist and
parse under `python3` + PyYAML (pinned validator, no node fallback - see the
parser disclosure). The scrape document must carry `global.scrape_interval`, a
`rule_files` entry naming `/etc/prometheus/alerts.yaml`, a `backend` job whose
`metrics_path` is `/metrics` and whose targets include the t41-pinned local
verification endpoint `127.0.0.1:8137`, and a `prometheus` self-scrape on
`127.0.0.1:9090`; EVERY target must match `127.0.0.1:<port>` so no remote
target, cloud exporter or hosted endpoint can slip in. `alerts.yaml` must parse
to a named rule group holding at least one alert rule. The in-fence positive
control feeds the same validator a document with NO `rule_files`, a
non-loopback target and no self-scrape, and requires rejection on all three
legs - so a GREEN cannot be vacuous.

```bash
bash -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac1 RED: python3 is not on PATH - this fence pins python3+PyYAML as its validator and deliberately has no node fallback (disclosed in the card): a skipped parse proves nothing, so the fence fails loudly instead"; exit 1; }; python3 -c "import yaml" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac1 RED: python3 is present but cannot import yaml (PyYAML) - install PyYAML into the interpreter, never edit the fence to work around a broken parser"; exit 1; }; printf "%s" "" | base64 -d > /tmp/t76_ac1_probe.py || { echo "ac1 RED: could not stage the probe to /tmp/t76_ac1_probe.py"; exit 1; }; python3 /tmp/t76_ac1_probe.py "$PWD" || { echo "ac1 RED: the probe exited non-zero - its own ac1 RED lines above name the failing leg; at BASE this is the expected RED because neither observability/prometheus.yml nor observability/alerts.yaml exists there"; exit 1; }; echo "ac1 GREEN: FILES PARSE AND SHAPE - both observability files exist and parse under python3+PyYAML, prometheus.yml carries global scrape_interval, the /etc/prometheus/alerts.yaml rule-file reference, the backend job on 127.0.0.1:8137 with metrics_path /metrics and the prometheus self-scrape on 127.0.0.1:9090 with every target loopback-only, and alerts.yaml parses with a named rule group holding alert rules (the no-rule_files / non-loopback / no-self-scrape negative control was rejected on all three legs)"'
```

### ac2 - the two required alerts exist with the pinned shape, and both are evaluable

`HighExpenseCreationFailures` (error-rate ratio over the two declared counters,
`for: 10m`, `severity: warning`) and `DBFallbackActive`
(`expr: db_fallback_active == 1`, `for: 5m`, `severity: critical` - the
supervisor-approved Option B form) must both exist with the full annotation set
`service`, `environment`, `version`, `owner`, `dashboard`, `summary`, and the
dashboard URL must be loopback. Beyond shape, the fence PROVES EVALUABILITY: a
minimal PromQL-subset evaluator in the probe runs both pinned expressions
against SYNTHESIZED series - `DBFallbackActive` must fire at `db_fallback_active
= 1` and must NOT fire at `0`; `HighExpenseCreationFailures` must fire at a
synthesized 0.3 ratio and must not fire at ~0.0067. This satisfies supervisor
condition 5 at parse level (no promtool on this host, no network download
permitted); end-to-end firing is demonstrated in the t84 drill via
`--simulate-fallback`. The in-fence positive control is a document with no
`for:`, a liveness `up == 0` expr and a missing annotation - all three legs
must reject it.

```bash
bash -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac2 RED: python3 is not on PATH - this fence pins python3+PyYAML as its validator and deliberately has no node fallback (disclosed in the card): a skipped parse proves nothing, so the fence fails loudly instead"; exit 1; }; python3 -c "import yaml" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac2 RED: python3 is present but cannot import yaml (PyYAML) - install PyYAML into the interpreter, never edit the fence to work around a broken parser"; exit 1; }; printf "%s" "" | base64 -d > /tmp/t76_ac2_probe.py || { echo "ac2 RED: could not stage the probe to /tmp/t76_ac2_probe.py"; exit 1; }; python3 /tmp/t76_ac2_probe.py "$PWD" || { echo "ac2 RED: the probe exited non-zero - its own ac2 RED lines above name the failing leg; at BASE this is the expected RED because neither observability/prometheus.yml nor observability/alerts.yaml exists there"; exit 1; }; echo "ac2 GREEN: ALERT SHAPES PINNED - HighExpenseCreationFailures (for 10m, severity warning, error-rate expr over the two declared counters) and DBFallbackActive (for 5m, severity critical, expr db_fallback_active == 1) are both defined with the full annotation set service/environment/version/owner/dashboard/summary and a loopback dashboard URL (the no-for / liveness-expr / missing-annotation negative control was rejected on all three legs)"'
```

Every metric name appearing in ANY `expr` must be a member of the
machine-readable `# # METRIC-INVENTORY:` comment block in the same file (the

EXACTLY the pinned four-name set with the pinned types:

bounded product-tree scan (see the supervisor decision above) must find NO
alert name and NO metric name outside the authority. Two controls keep the leg

a planted file carrying an alert name plus a `# TYPE` line must be FOUND by the
same scan in a throwaway tree - otherwise a zero-hit scan proves nothing. This
scan leg is a point-in-time authority check and is declared NON-APPENDABLE:
when t79 later lands legitimate inventory code it will match, so the
orchestrator must not append it to the merge-test index.

### ac4 - the alert the incident record quotes is byte-stable

The `DBFallbackActive` rule's canonical form (sorted-key, compact-separator
JSON of the parsed rule) must hash to the pinned digest

    sha256:631fff291c752ec026e7f585ccd3ad57f71dd868eb0ca94745a428aa49daeca0

canonical form: {"alert":"DBFallbackActive","annotations":{"dashboard":"http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/expense-tracker/expense-tracker","environment":"development","owner":"tw097","service":"expense-tracker-api","summary":"the database fallback latch is engaged and the API is serving from the fallback store","version":"1.0.0"},"expr":"db_fallback_active == 1","for":"5m","labels":{"severity":"critical"}}

matching any string. t83 byte-copies this entry into its incident `alert.json`
and t85 names the alert in `ops/diagnosis.md`; any change here forces a
t83/t84 re-check, which is what the pin is for.

fences and are appendable candidates; **ac3's product-tree scan leg is ALSO
NON-APPENDABLE** - it asserts a point-in-time absence, and t79's own legitimate

disclosed-cause route applies: report PASS-with-disclosed-cause with the
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <offending commit> HEAD` provenance for each
forgiven path, do NOT edit the fence, the BASE or the allow-list.

**Parser disclosure.** Every YAML leg runs through `python3` + PyYAML, pinned
as the single validator, and FAILS LOUDLY when python3 is absent or PyYAML is
not importable. There is deliberately NO node/js-yaml fallback (simpler than
t75's chain and stated here so nobody "fixes" the fence): a skipped parse would
prove nothing about a rules file whose whole job is being read correctly. A RED
for "parser missing" is an environment fix (install PyYAML - measured 6.0.1
importable on the grooming host), never a licence to edit the fence.

**No-live-server disclosure.** No fence starts Prometheus or Alertmanager,
requires a docker daemon, or makes a network call. `promtool` is not installed
on the grooming host and no fence downloads it; ac2's evaluability proof is a
parse-level evaluator over synthesized series, and end-to-end firing is
demonstrated in the t84 drill via `--simulate-fallback`.

**Foreign worktree disclosure.** The grooming worktree carries in-flight
changes by OTHER roles (`incident-response/README.md`,
`incident-response/collect-evidence.sh`, `.pi/subagents/`,
`docs/state/outputs/`, `scratch/`). This groom touched NONE of them - its only
writes are the card, its groom mirror, this handoff and `build/t76/` scratch
(`build/` is gitignored). All are disclosed-path output in ac5 terms.

## Constraints (hard - the builder may not drop any of these)

- Exactly 2 product files: `observability/prometheus.yml`,
  `observability/alerts.yaml` (max_files=4 is the ceiling, this card uses 2).
  Plus the builder card and its groom mirror.
- `observability/alerts.yaml` is the ONE alert-name and metric-name authority
  for the milestone. This card invents names; no other card may. The inventory
  is exactly the four declared names - adding a fifth name here is a card FAIL.
- NO edit to `observability/compose.yaml` or `observability/README.md` (t75's
  files, blob-pinned by ac5). The missing `alerts.yaml` rule-file mount is
  reported as a follow-up, never fixed here - a second writer on one file is
  the phase_12 lesson.
- No new port, no new service, no dependency addition, no backend code.
- Scrape targets are loopback only (`127.0.0.1:8137` backend,
  `127.0.0.1:9090` self-scrape). No remote scrape target, no cloud exporter,
  no hosted Grafana, no hosted endpoint anywhere in either file.
- `for:` durations are explicit: `10m` for `HighExpenseCreationFailures`,
  `5m` for `DBFallbackActive` (the operator-approved value the fence pins).
- `DBFallbackActive` reads `db_fallback_active == 1` (Option B). Writing
  `up{job="backend"} == 0` or any other liveness form here is a card FAIL - it
  misnames a liveness rule as a fallback rule.
- No live Prometheus/Alertmanager execution in any fence; no network call; no
  promtool download.
- `openapi.yaml` untouched (FROZEN). The `/metrics` endpoint this scrape config
  reads is t78's; its contract exemption is recorded in t78's card, not here.
- Both files pure ASCII, LF endings, 2-space indent, no tabs
  (docs/coding_standards.md).
- The `DBFallbackActive` entry is byte-frozen by the pinned digest: changing
  any key or value forces a t83/t84 re-check.

## Out of scope

- The `alerts.yaml` rule-file MOUNT into the Prometheus container. t75's
  `observability/compose.yaml` mounts only `prometheus.yml`, so the
  `rule_files` path this card declares is not yet materialised in the
  container. Fixing it means editing t75's file, which the second-writer rule
  forbids; it belongs to whichever later card is granted ownership of
  `observability/compose.yaml` (or to the t88 closeout as a recorded gap).
  Consequence if nobody picks it up: Prometheus evaluates zero rules.
- Emitting the four declared metrics. That is t79 in
  `backend/app/telemetry.py` (and t79's own extraction AC fails if
  `db_fallback_active` is not emitted).
- Dashboard panels (`observability/dashboard.json`) and the collector

- The incident `alert.json` byte-copy (t83), the diagnosis rewrite that names

- Alertmanager receiver configuration, remote write, hosted Grafana, and any
